title: Church Ordinances
definition: Church Ordinances are the visible practices Christ gave His Church, especially baptism and the Lord’s Supper, to proclaim and remember the Gospel.
summary: Church Ordinances are the visible practices Christ gave His Church, especially baptism and the Lord’s Supper, to proclaim and remember the Gospel.
christFocus: Jesus commands His Church to baptize disciples and remember His death, using visible signs to point His people back to His saving work.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Ordinances are not empty traditions when practiced by faith according to Scripture. Baptism visibly identifies believers with Christ, and the Lord’s Supper visibly proclaims His death until He comes.

These practices help the Church remember the Gospel with the body as well as the mind. They preach through water, bread, and cup that salvation is found in Christ, not in human achievement.

The ordinances also mark the Church as a people gathered around Christ’s command. They belong to discipleship, worship, community, and public witness.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Some believers come from backgrounds where religious rituals felt confusing, lifeless, or controlling. Scripture gives ordinances as Gospel-centered gifts, not as burdens detached from Christ.

This doctrine helps keep the Church from becoming purely verbal or purely experiential. Christ gave visible practices to strengthen visible faith.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Practice and receive the ordinances with Scripture-shaped understanding. Let baptism and the Lord’s Supper point you to Christ, strengthen your faith, and remind the Church of the Gospel it is called to proclaim.
